Benefits of Working With a Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Lawyer in Dubuque: How We Can Help

While some individuals attempt to navigate bankruptcy cases alone, working with a Chapter 13 lawyer can deliver peace of mind and practical advantages. At Henkels & Baker, we want you to feel informed and empowered, especially when your family’s home or future is on the line.

Here’s how our hands-on approach can help:

Protection Against Foreclosure

If you’ve fallen behind on your mortgage, filing Chapter 13 can halt Foreclosure in Iowa and create a manageable path to catch up on missed payments. We’ve seen many clients save their homes with timely legal action. Because we emphasize open communication, we’ll keep you updated on every step so court proceedings never blindside you.

We know how important it is to protect what you’ve worked hard for. Chapter 13 often allows you to keep cars and other essential property. Developing a payment plan that fits your real-life budget can be complex. Few things are as draining as unending calls and letters from creditors. When we file your Chapter 13 petition, those contacts typically have to stop. Should creditors violate the automatic stay, we’re here to help enforce your rights. The relief from harassment often feels like the first real step toward reclaiming your life.

Our reach goes beyond Dubuque city limits. We serve clients across parts of Iowa, Wisconsin, and Illinois, within roughly 100 miles of our office at 40 Main St., Suite 100. If you are nearby and need a Chapter 13 bankruptcy lawyer Dubuque residents rely on, we are close.

When you are ready to talk, we are here to listen without judgment and help you find the clearest path forward.

How Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Works in Dubuque

Filing for Chapter 13 bankruptcy helps you reorganize your debt while keeping your essential assets. However, to succeed, you need to follow every step carefully. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we guide you through the process, ensuring you meet all legal requirements and feel confident about your financial future.

Step 1: Personalized Consultation and Financial Review

We start with a private meeting to review your finances, income, debts, expenses, and legal issues like lawsuits or foreclosure notices. During this session, we also discuss your goals. Do you want to save your home, stop creditor harassment, or simplify multiple debts into one payment? After reviewing your financial situation and eligibility, we confirm whether Chapter 13 bankruptcy is the right option.

Step 2: Preparing and Filing Your Bankruptcy Petition

The law requires that you complete a credit counseling course before filing. Then, we can collect all necessary documents, such as tax returns, pay stubs, bank statements, loan information, and asset valuations. We prepare your Chapter 13 bankruptcy petition and a detailed repayment plan using this information. 

Once we file your case with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Iowa, an automatic stay immediately stops most creditor actions, such as foreclosure, repossession, wage garnishments, and collection calls.

Step 4: 341 Meeting of Creditors

About 30 days after filing, you attend a 341 meeting of creditors. This is a required but informal hearing where the bankruptcy trustee reviews your case and asks questions about your financial situation. Creditors can also attend and ask questions, though they rarely do. We prepare you for this meeting and attend with you to ensure the process runs smoothly. 

Step 5: Plan Confirmation Hearing

Six to eight weeks after the 341 meeting, the bankruptcy court holds a confirmation hearing to review your repayment plan. The judge ensures that your plan meets all legal requirements. If the trustee or creditors raise concerns, we negotiate changes to the plan to resolve issues and secure approval. We work hard to protect your interests and create a manageable repayment plan. 

Step 6: Making Payments and Monitoring Progress

Once the court approves your plan, you start making monthly payments to the bankruptcy trustee. The trustee distributes these payments to your creditors according to the plan. If you are behind on your mortgage, the plan may include catch-up payments to stop foreclosure. We continue to monitor your case and help you adjust if your financial situation changes. 

Step 7: Completion and Discharge

After you complete your repayment plan, which typically lasts three to five years, and a debtor education course, the court issues a discharge order. This discharge wipes out most remaining unsecured debts, such as credit card bills and medical debts, and prevents creditors from trying to collect on those debts in the future.

At Henkels & Baker, PC, our experienced Bankruptcy Lawyers in Iowa are with you every step of the way, ensuring you have the support and guidance you need to complete the Chapter 13 process and achieve financial freedom.

blocks.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Chapter 13 Bankruptcy

items.q: What is Chapter 13 bankruptcy in Iowa, and how does it help?
items.a: Chapter 13, often called the “wage earner’s plan,” allows people with regular income to reorganize their debts over a three- to five-year repayment plan—without selling assets. Unlike Chapter 7, it helps you keep your home, car, and other essentials, while providing temporary relief by stopping wage garnishments, creditor calls, repossessions, and foreclosure.

items.q: Who is eligible to file for Chapter 13 in Dubuque?
items.a:
To qualify, you need to :

  • Have both secured and unsecured debts below set federal limits;
  • Have stable income (from wages, self-employment, benefits, etc.) to make monthly plan payments;
  • Complete a required credit counseling session before filing;
  • Be current on income tax filings for the past several years.

items.q: What debts are paid during Chapter 13 in Iowa?
items.a: Your repayment plan should fully pay priority debts (such as taxes, child support, and other legal obligations), secured debts up to collateral value (like a mortgage or car loan).  Unsecured debts, such as credit card balances or medical bills, are generally paid at least as much as they would under Chapter 7—often meaning partial or even full discharge of remaining balances when the plan is completed.

items.q: How is my monthly Chapter 13 payment calculated?
items.a: Your Chapter 13 payment depends on your income, reasonable living expenses, the types of debts you owe, and the amount creditors must receive under bankruptcy law. Your repayment plan may also include past-due mortgage payments, car loans, and certain priority debts. A Chapter 13 bankruptcy attorney in Dubuque can review your financial situation and help determine what a proposed monthly payment could look like.

items.q: Can Chapter 13 bankruptcy help me keep my home if I am behind on mortgage payments?
items.a: Chapter 13 bankruptcy may help you avoid foreclosure by allowing you to catch up on overdue mortgage payments through a court-approved repayment plan. However, you generally must continue making your regular mortgage payments while completing the plan. Filing before a foreclosure sale is especially important because the timing of your case can affect your available options.

items.q: When do I start making Chapter 13 bankruptcy payments?
items.a: Chapter 13 plan payments generally must begin within 30 days after filing your bankruptcy petition, even if the court has not yet approved your repayment plan. Missing required payments can put your case at risk. Your attorney can explain the payment schedule and help you prepare for your financial obligations.

items.q: What happens if I lose my job or my income changes during Chapter 13?
items.a: If your financial circumstances change during Chapter 13 bankruptcy, you may be able to request a modification of your repayment plan. A job loss, reduced income, or unexpected expenses can affect your ability to make payments. Modifications are not automatic, so contacting your attorney promptly is important to explore available options and avoid potential dismissal of your case.
